mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has improved by 3.6 percentage points from t-3w to t-0w, signaling restoration of commuting infrastructure. This sustained recovery in transit access will drive retail-and-recreation mobility upward over the next four weeks as commuters regain access to shopping districts.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT improved from -31.9 to -28.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over next 28 days does not exceed RETAIL_REC mean over last 28 days, or TRANSIT reverses to decline below -30 within two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 9.9 to 9.1 percentage points above baseline, indicating reduced home confinement. This behavioral shift toward outdoor activity will translate to increased retail-and-recreation visits as people resume discretionary spending patterns over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined from 9.9 to 9.1 over four weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility increases above 10.0 in the next two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to increase relative to baseline mean of last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: When GROCERY_PHARM mobility falls below -14.5 percent (threshold crossed at t-0w: -14.6), it signals reduced essential-goods shopping frequency, indicating consumers are consolidating trips and may redirect freed time to retail-recreation venues. This substitution effect will elevate RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM rebounds above -14.0 within one week, or RETAIL_REC does not increase relative to its four-week mean in the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered 14.9 percentage points from t-3w (-58.3) to t-0w (-43.4), indicating seasonal outdoor activity resumption. This outdoor-activity surge will spill over into adjacent retail-recreation venues (markets, outdoor shopping areas) within one week, driving RETAIL_REC upward.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by more than 10 percentage points week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -58.3 to -43.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: PARKS mobility reverses to decline below -50 within one week, or RETAIL_REC does not show measurable increase in the immediate following week.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in TRANSIT (+3.6 points) and decline in RESIDENTIAL confinement (−0.8 points) creates a compounding effect: restored commuting access combined with reduced home-staying behavior will jointly amplify retail-recreation mobility over the next four weeks. Neither signal alone is sufficient; both must persist.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT improves AND RESIDENTIAL declines simultaneously
failure_condition: Either TRANSIT or RESIDENTIAL reverses direction within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its four-week baseline mean over the next 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized at -29.1 percent (minimal change from -31.1 four weeks prior), indicating workplace restrictions remain constant. Under this regime of stable workplace constraints, retail-recreation mobility will remain suppressed as consumer spending power and commuting frequency remain constrained over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES remains within ±2 percentage points of current level
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES at -29.1 in t-0w, -31.1 in t-3w
failure_condition: WORKPLACES improves by more than 5 percentage points within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC increases above its four-week mean despite stable workplace constraints.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility remains severely depressed at -43.4 percent despite recent recovery, indicating outdoor-activity venues are still substantially constrained. This persistent parks suppression signals broader mobility restrictions remain in force, which will continue to suppress retail-recreation mobility over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: PARKS improves above -35 percent within one week, or RETAIL_REC increases by more than 2 percentage points in the following two weeks.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction of persistently low GROCERY_PHARM (-14.6) with stagnant WORKPLACES (-29.1) indicates consumers are both reducing essential-goods trips and maintaining low workplace presence. This dual constraint on consumer mobility and income-earning activity will suppress retail-recreation spending over the next four weeks as purchasing power and trip frequency remain depressed.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM below -14.0 AND WORKPLACES below -28.0 simultaneously
failure_condition: Either GROCERY_PHARM or WORKPLACES improves by more than 3 percentage points within two weeks, or RETAIL_REC exceeds its four-week mean over the next 28 days.
